root_system.title: Root-Zone Interaction Lab
root_system.principle: Roots respond to water, oxygen, ionic concentration, pH, temperature, media structure, and biology as one interacting system. A single root-zone reading rarely explains plant response by itself.

states.label: Drying
states.effect: Water availability is falling; root water uptake becomes harder as the substrate dries.

states.label: Balanced
states.effect: Water and air-filled pore space can coexist when media structure and irrigation timing are appropriate.

states.label: Saturated
states.effect: Excess water can displace air from pore space and reduce oxygen diffusion to roots.

states.label: Low
states.effect: Low oxygen can constrain root respiration and reduce active uptake processes.

states.label: Adequate
states.effect: Adequate oxygen supports respiration, new root growth, and active ion transport.

states.label: Lower
states.effect: Lower ionic concentration reduces osmotic resistance but may also reflect low nutrient availability depending on system and stage.

states.label: Moderate
states.effect: Interpret EC against source water, feed strength, runoff or pore-water method, crop stage, and recent dryback.

states.label: Higher
states.effect: Higher ionic concentration raises osmotic pressure and can make water uptake more difficult even when media looks wet.

states.label: Off target
states.effect: pH outside the useful range for a given substrate can shift nutrient solubility and uptake, but the correct target depends on media and method.

states.label: In context
states.effect: Use substrate-specific pH targets and measurement methods rather than one universal number.

stem_vascular.title: Vascular Transport Lab
stem_vascular.principle: Xylem and phloem are different transport tissues. Xylem mainly carries water and mineral nutrients from roots toward transpiring tissues; phloem distributes sugars and other transported compounds between source and sink tissues.

channels.label: Xylem
channels.driver: Water-potential gradients, cohesion-tension, root and hydraulic forces
channels.note: Transpiration strongly influences bulk xylem flow, but transport is part of a continuous soil-plant-atmosphere hydraulic system.

channels.label: Phloem
channels.cargo: Sugars and other transported organic compounds
channels.driver: Pressure-flow generated by loading and unloading between source and sink tissues
channels.note: Whole-plant phloem transport can occur in different directions at the same time because different sieve pathways serve different sources and sinks.

flowers.title: Flower Development Lab
flowers.principle: Flower development is a sequence rather than a single 'flowering' state. Timing varies with genetics and environment, so structural changes are more useful than fixed calendar weeks.

stages.label: Initiation
stages.visible: Preflowers and reproductive structures become easier to distinguish at nodes.
stages.biology: Meristems shift toward reproductive development under genetic and environmental control.

stages.label: Early flower
stages.visible: Bracts and stigmas increase while clusters begin forming along flowering sites.
stages.biology: Cell division and floral organ development are rapid; stretch and new reproductive growth may overlap.

stages.label: Flower building
stages.visible: Floral clusters enlarge and bracts accumulate; glandular trichome density becomes increasingly obvious.
stages.biology: Carbon allocation to reproductive tissues rises while leaves continue supporting photosynthesis and transport.

stages.label: Ripening
stages.visible: New floral expansion slows relative to maturation; stigmas and trichomes show mixed age states.
stages.biology: Secondary metabolite composition, resin gland condition, and tissue senescence continue changing.

stages.label: Late maturation / senescence
stages.visible: Older tissues may fade and many floral structures show advanced age, but appearance varies strongly by genotype and conditions.
stages.biology: Developmental aging continues; stress, disease, pollination, and environment can mimic or accelerate some late-stage appearances.

observe: trichomes on bracts rather than sugar leaves

trichomes_resin.title: Trichome Microscope Lab
trichomes_resin.principle: Trichome appearance is useful developmental evidence, not a standalone chemical assay. Judge comparable glandular trichomes on representative flower bracts and combine microscopy with cultivar history and whole-flower maturity.

types.label: Bulbous
types.structure: Tiny glandular trichomes with a small head and short base; difficult to evaluate with low magnification.

types.label: Capitate-sessile
types.structure: Glandular head sits close to the epidermis on a very short stalk.

types.label: Capitate-stalked
types.structure: Prominent stalk supports a glandular head; these become abundant on female floral tissues and are common targets for maturity inspection.

appearance.label: Clear / translucent
appearance.meaning: Often associated with younger gland heads, but illumination, focus, tissue location, and optics can change apparent clarity.

appearance.label: Cloudy / opaque
appearance.meaning: Often seen as glandular contents and optical properties change during maturation; it does not directly reveal a laboratory potency value.

appearance.label: Amber / darkened
appearance.meaning: Can increase with aging and oxidation, but ambering is not uniform across the plant and may appear earlier on exposed leaf trichomes.

observe: avoid relying on sugar-leaf trichomes alone

sex_pollen_seed.title: Reproductive Structure Lab
sex_pollen_seed.principle: Sex expression is identified from reproductive structures, not overall plant shape. Inspect nodes and flowers closely and distinguish normal female, male, and mixed/intersex structures.

structures.label: Female flower
features: glandular trichomes increase during flower development
structures.note: A single pair of stigmas at a node can be an early female cue, but inspect multiple sites as the plant develops.

structures.label: Male flower
structures.note: Immature structures can be easy to misread; shape and development over time help confirm identification.

structures.label: Mixed / intersex expression
features: male reproductive structures may occur on otherwise female flowering tissue
anthers can appear inside or among female floral structures
structures.note: Record exact location, timing, frequency, genetics, and recent stress rather than assuming one universal cause.

structures.label: Seed development
features: seed coat and embryo mature over time
structures.note: Seed formation changes resource allocation and is evidence that successful pollination occurred earlier.
